newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile agriculture exports to Canada seen booming.
newsitem.headline: Chile agriculture exports to Canada seen booming.

text.p: Chile's agricultural exports to Canada are likely to rise sharply as a result of the bilateral free trade agreement which came into force last week, said Canadian ambassador Marc Lortie.
"For Chileans the strongest growth sector is without doubt the agricultural industry," Lortie told Reuters at the signing of a bilateral agricultural co-operation agreement.
"There is tremendous demand in Canada for Chilean wine and fresh fruit."
The free trade agreement swept away tariffs on the bulk of Chilean agricultural exports to Canada.
Duties, however, on Canadian exports to Chile including wheat and sugar will fall gradually over the next 18 years to protect Chile's farming industry.
Chilean officials have said that bilateral trade, currently around $670 million a year, may rise by five-fold over the next decade.
"We agree, but responsibility lies with private companies. Chileans must come to Canada to see what opportunities exist," he said.
Chile's exports to Canada came to $300 million last year, with the agriculture sector accounting for 42 percent.
